assessment.reason: The plan follows the supplied authority, preserves all seven concrete transition tuples, and distinguishes Close-to-summary from Back-to-introduction-h1 focus. It treats the target as a fixture rather than project authority.

The plan requires genuine sequential Tab from the observed restored summary focus to Back, focused Back before Enter, actual Enter activation, and resulting introduction-h1 focus. It expressly rejects click, direct focus, screenshots alone and repaired focus as substitutes.

The plan specifies observable unanswered state, no prohibited actions, pre-navigation origin and method prevention, redirects/subresources, blocked execution if prevention is unavailable, and conditional analytics evidence. It does not claim a working browser guard. The retained harness probe separately records blocked network and immutable inputs.

The plan calls the target a reconstructed fixture, identifies its omissions as documentary, and expressly leaves current deployment behavior unknown. It separates local checker success, document coverage, browser acceptance failure and blocked/unobserved evidence.

The correct checker command has captured exit-zero output, while the planned document work has full transition-tuple review, eight-check mapping and meaningful positive/negative Gherkin. Proposed future browser/guard checks are labeled unexecuted. Structural lint is correctly bounded.

The selected outcome is one document plan supported by the actual supplied target/source differences. It includes the missing summary key cycle and keyboard Back, preserves distinct focus and boundaries, and justifies excluding application/harness changes. The actual local consistency check supports source consistency only.

comparison.reason: Separate evaluators and verifier retained task/coverage observations. One observation on related known tasks and visible conditions does not establish a comparative winner; live deployment comparability is unverified for UX.

limitations: One observation on a related known task, not a general benefit benchmark.
